_readme: SEMANTIC LAYER — Olist E-Commerce Project. OpenCode reads this file alongside CLAUDE.md at the start of every session. It defines every table, join, field meaning, and canonical metric so you never have to re-explain the data model.
critical_rules: ALWAYS use customer_unique_id for customer counts — never customer_id (customer_id inflates count because one person can have multiple IDs)
ALWAYS filter to order_status = 'delivered' for revenue and satisfaction analysis
ALWAYS use payment_value from payments table for revenue — not price from order_items (price is item-level only)
NEVER modify files in 01_Raw_Data/ — read only
Currency is BRL throughout — no conversion

olist_orders_dataset.role: central fact table — every order placed on the platform

key_columns.order_id: unique identifier for each order — use this to join every other table
key_columns.customer_id: WARNING: do not use for customer counts — use customer_unique_id from customers table instead
key_columns.order_status: delivered | shipped | canceled | invoiced | processing | unavailable | created — filter to delivered for all revenue analysis
key_columns.order_purchase_timestamp: when the customer placed the order — use this as the primary date for time-series analysis
key_columns.order_estimated_delivery_date: promised delivery date — compare to delivered date for on-time calculation

derived_columns_to_calculate.days_early_or_late: order_estimated_delivery_date minus order_delivered_customer_date — positive = early, negative = late
derived_columns_to_calculate.is_late: 1 if days_early_or_late is negative (arrived after promised date), else 0

olist_order_payments_dataset.role: how each order was paid and for how much
olist_order_payments_dataset.row_grain: one row per payment — WARNING: one order can have multiple rows (split payments)

key_columns.payment_value: THIS IS THE REVENUE COLUMN — use SUM(payment_value) grouped by order_id for total order revenue

olist_order_payments_dataset.aggregation_note: Always aggregate to one row per order_id before joining: total_payment_value = SUM(payment_value)

olist_order_items_dataset.role: what was in each order at item level
olist_order_items_dataset.row_grain: one row per item — one order can have multiple rows

key_columns.price: item price — NOT the same as payment_value. Use payment_value for total revenue analysis.

olist_order_items_dataset.aggregation_note: Aggregate to one row per order_id: item_count = COUNT, total_items_price = SUM(price), total_freight = SUM(freight_value)

key_columns.review_score: integer 1-5 — 1 and 2 are negative reviews, 4 and 5 are positive
key_columns.review_comment_message: written comment — 41% of reviews have one, 59% are blank

key_columns.customer_id: WARNING: inflated — one real customer can have multiple customer_id values across different orders
key_columns.customer_unique_id: USE THIS for all customer counts — represents one real person
key_columns.customer_state: two-letter Brazilian state code — SP is São Paulo, RJ is Rio de Janeiro

key_columns.product_category_name: category in Portuguese — always join to translation table for English
key_columns.category_english: English translation — use this for all analysis and reporting

olist_products_dataset.known_issue: 610 products have null product_category_name — these are labelled 'uncategorized' in the clean file, not dropped

product_category_name_translation.role: Portuguese to English category name mapping
product_category_name_translation.join: join to products on product_category_name to get category_english

olist_geolocation_dataset.role: GPS coordinates for Brazilian zip codes
olist_geolocation_dataset.known_issue: raw file has 1M+ rows — always use geolocation_clean.csv which has one row per zip_code_prefix

olist_master.role: PRE-JOINED master table — use this for all analysis instead of joining raw tables manually
olist_master.note: already contains all key columns from orders, customers, payments (aggregated), items (aggregated), reviews

joins.primary_join_path: orders → customers via customer_id | orders → payments via order_id | orders → order_items via order_id | orders → reviews via order_id | order_items → products via product_id | order_items → sellers via seller_id | products → translation via product_category_name
joins.shortcut: Use olist_master.csv — it already contains all joins for delivered orders

total_revenue.formula: SUM(payment_value) from payments table, joined to orders, filtered to order_status = 'delivered'
total_revenue.do_not_use: SUM(price) from order_items — this is item-level only, misses vouchers and multi-payment orders

repeat_purchase_rate.formula: COUNT(customers with more than 1 order) / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) * 100
repeat_purchase_rate.context: Olist baseline is approximately 3% — critically low, major strategic finding

on_time_delivery_rate.formula: COUNT(orders where order_delivered_customer_date <= order_estimated_delivery_date) / COUNT(total delivered orders) * 100
on_time_delivery_rate.benchmark: 90% industry standard — flag if below this

avg_review_score.benchmark: 4.0 is healthy marketplace threshold — flag if below this

revenue_by_category.formula: SUM(price) from order_items, joined to products for category_english
revenue_by_category.note: Use price here (item level) not payment_value — this is category attribution not total revenue

common_questions_and_how_to_answer_them.What is the repeat rate?: COUNT customers with order_count > 1 / total unique customers from entity_behaviour analysis
common_questions_and_how_to_answer_them.Which state has most revenue?: GROUP BY customer_state, SUM(total_payment_value) from olist_master.csv
common_questions_and_how_to_answer_them.Are deliveries on time?: AVG(is_late) from olist_master.csv — 0 = on time, 1 = late
common_questions_and_how_to_answer_them.Which category sells most?: JOIN order_items to products_clean on product_id, GROUP BY category_english, SUM(price)
common_questions_and_how_to_answer_them.How long does delivery take?: AVG(delivery_days) from olist_master.csv, optionally GROUP BY customer_state
